business.title: Beyond years of schooling: Genetic associations across educational milestones in two Norwegian cohorts
business.desc: Author summary Genetic studies of education usually summarize attainment as years of schooling. Yet people do not simply accumulate years; they progress through credentials such as high school, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees. We analyzed these milestones in two Norwegian cohorts containing more than 120,000 genotyped adults and nearly 9,000 twins. Among high-school graduates, analyses based on common DNA variants and genetic scores showed the clearest signal when comparing those who attained at least a bachelor’s degree with those whose highest credential was high school. Signals were weaker at the ends of the sequence, but those comparisons also had different structures: high-school completion is nearly universal in Norway, while doctoral progression is assessed among people who have already passed several earlier milestones. Twin analyses produced their highest heritability estimate for high-school completion, although uncertainty was substantial. These findings show that genetic results depend on the educational contrast being studied and on who is included in the comparison group. A single years-based measure compresses these differences, and one additional year should not be assumed to represent the same educational step throughout the sequence. Treating education as milestones provides a clearer basis for interpreting genetic studies of education.
